title: A wrong key or fact fails the item
statement: Every part of an item, shown to students or not, must be factually right and agree with the key, since a wrong key or fact anywhere fails the whole item.
example: Over 1,124 graded rows, an item whose factual accuracy scored zero passed 0% of the time.
detail: A criteria pack built from 1,124 graded rows of one AP model found that when factual accuracy or source quality scored zero, the row passed 0% of the time, and marked both as must-pass gates (the pass-criteria `README.md`, lines 12 and 72). The AP evaluator's scoring table counts a wrong answer or false claim as a critical failure, and with one critical failure an item scores 0.84 at most, below the 0.85 where acceptable begins (`_base_evaluation.txt`, lines 232, 244, 250 and 262). Being right and agreeing with the key applies to explanations, hints, feedback, model answers, marking notes and source details alike, and a failed source fails the item as surely as a wrong key, however good the rest is.
against: outside that field, published practice uses a human-in-the-loop acceptance rate with no hard threshold (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`). In an earlier AP evaluator one non-critical failure still scored 0.85 to 0.89, a pass, and only a critical failure such as a wrong fact always failed (`icloud-work/evaluator/docs/EVALUATION_PROCESS.md`, lines 97-123), so whether every other flaw sinks an item depends on the grader. The rise from 0.33 to 0.97 came under a release that also tightened leak checks, so the explanation fix alone is not shown.

This is NOT just overall_score ≥ 0.85. An item can score 0.92 overall and still hard-fail if a single hard-fail dimension drops below 1.0. The hard-fail dimensions are binary gates — they must all be perfect.

These dimensions must score 1.0 for the question to pass. A score below 1.0 results in automatic failure regardless of overall score.
- Factual claims, answer keys, rationales, feedback, and support fields all count for `factual_accuracy`.
- The keyed answer must be factually correct and internally consistent with all explanations, hints, feedback, and additional details.

Answer explanations must not contradict option text.
The practical rule for the generator is: **do not aim for “mostly good”; produce a checklist-complete item with no score-zero openings.**
